Conceptual Foundations
======================

The European Interoperability Reference Architecture, EIRA©
-----------------------------------------------------------

The **European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA©)** is a
**four-view reference architecture** designed to deliver interoperable
digital public services across borders and sectors in the European
Union. It serves as a comprehensive framework that defines the required
capabilities for promoting interoperability through a structured set of
**Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs)**.

 

EIRA© provides a blueprint with recommended best practices, standards,
and guidelines for designing and implementing systems that are
efficient, scalable, and interoperable. It operates as a **technology
and product-neutral, service-oriented architecture (SOA)** that uses
ArchiMate® as its modelling notation.

The eGovernment European Reference Architecture, eGovERA©
---------------------------------------------------------

The eGovernment European Reference Architecture (eGovERA) provides
further granularity and domain focus extension of the European
Interoperability Reference Architecture. Whilst EIRA establishes a
foundational vocabulary of Architecture Building Blocks at the
meta-concept level (level 1 granularity), eGovERA delivers level 2 and
further granularity by expanding these building blocks into detailed
architecture patterns and implementation guidance. This hierarchical
relationship ensures that eGovERA maintains full alignment with EIRA's
core principles and structure whilst offering the additional specificity
required for practical solution design and implementation.

Purposes of EIRA and eGovERA
----------------------------

The European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) and the
eGovernment European Reference Architecture (eGovERA) extension share a
common mission: to enable European public administrations to design and
deliver digital public services that are interoperable by design,
efficient in operation, and capable of functioning effectively across
organisational and national boundaries. Both architectures serve as
structured frameworks that guide the analysis, design, and
implementation of solutions aligned with the principles and
recommendations of the European Interoperability Framework.

Core Shared Purposes
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

At their foundation, both EIRA and eGovERA fulfil three essential
purposes for European public administrations:

**Guidance for solution development:** Both architectures provide
systematic guidance for creating digital public services that meet
specific policy objectives and user needs. They offer structured
approaches to analyse requirements, identify necessary capabilities, and
design solutions that address the multidimensional nature of
interoperability challenges. This guidance helps public administrations
navigate the complexity of cross-border and cross-sector service
delivery by providing clear frameworks for architectural
decision-making.

**Best practices and standards:** EIRA and eGovERA embody accumulated
knowledge from successful digital public service implementations across
Europe. They incorporate best practices, reference to established
standards and specifications, and architectural principles that promote
the creation of systems that are efficient, scalable, secure, and
interoperable. By consolidating this knowledge into reusable
architectural components, both architectures enable public
administrations to benefit from proven approaches rather than repeatedly
solving similar problems independently.

**Common language:** Perhaps most fundamentally, both architectures
establish a shared vocabulary and conceptual framework for discussing
digital public services and their interoperability requirements. This
common language, expressed through Architecture Building Blocks
organised according to the LOST views (Legal, Organisational, Semantic,
and Technical), facilitates communication between diverse stakeholders
-including policy makers, enterprise architects, solution designers,
technical implementers, and procurement specialists. By providing this
shared architectural vocabulary, EIRA and eGovERA reduce complexity,
enhance coordination between organisations, and lower costs by enabling
reuse of both architectural knowledge and solution components.

Unit of analysis
----------------

The unit of analysis for both the European Interoperability Reference
Architecture (EIRA) and the eGovernment European Reference Architecture
(eGovERA) is **an European public administration Interoperable Solution
encompassing an interoperability enabling legal solution component, an
interoperability enabling organizational/governance solution component,
an interoperable semantic solution component, an Interoperable digital
solution component (Digital Public Service**\  [1]_Included), and an
interoperability enabling technical infrastructure solution component.
As defined by the European Commission, Digital Public Services refers to
the use of technologies to provide and deliver services at all
jurisdictional levels (European, national, regional, and local) to
citizens, businesses, and other public administrations. By adopting the
**European public administration Interoperable Solution** as the
fundamental unit of analysis, both reference architectures ensure that
interoperability considerations are addressed holistically, encompassing
the complete service delivery context rather than focusing narrowly on
isolated solution components.

An **European public administration Interoperable Solution** represents
the end-to-end capability through which a public administration fulfils
a public policy objective using digital means. This encompasses not
merely the technological systems involved, but the entire service
delivery mechanism across all dimensions required for effective
interoperable operation. Analysing **European public administration
Interoperable Solution**\ s through EIRA and eGovERA requires systematic
consideration of four interrelated dimensions aligned with the European
Interoperability Framework: Legal, Organisational, Semantic and
Technical (application and infrastructure).

By maintaining the **European public administration Interoperable
Solution** as the unit of analysis across all four dimensions, EIRA and
eGovERA ensure that architecture work systematically addresses the
complete interoperability challenge. This **holistic approach prevents
the common pitfall of addressing technical interoperability in isolation
whilst neglecting equally critical legal, organisational, or semantic
considerations** that determine whether services can genuinely operate
effectively across borders and organisational boundaries.

Use cases for the Reference Architectures
-----------------------------------------

Both the European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) and the
eGovernment European Reference Architecture (eGovERA) serve two primary
and complementary use cases that support the complete lifecycle of
digital public service development: Analysis and Design. These use cases
represent distinct but closely interconnected activities that guide
public administrations from initial service conception through to
implementable solution architecture, ensuring that interoperability
considerations are systematically addressed throughout the development
process.

- **Analysis Use Case:** The Analysis use case refers to the systematic
  activity of examining and documenting the requirements needed for the
  provision and delivery of digital public services that are
  interoperable by design. The output of the Analysis use case is a
  comprehensive understanding of interoperability requirements,
  documented through identification of relevant Architecture Building
  Blocks, specification of functional and non-functional requirements,
  and articulation of constraints and dependencies that will guide
  subsequent design decisions.

- **Design Use Case:** The Design use case refers to the realisation of
  analysis requirements through the identification and specification of
  solutions that will be implemented to address the needs and
  requirements gathered during analysis. The output of the Design use
  case is a documented solution architecture that specifies the mapping
  of Solution Building Blocks to Architecture Building Blocks, the
  selected standards and interoperability specifications, the definition
  of interfaces and integration points, and implementation guidance for
  development or deployment teams, providing a clear blueprint for how
  the digital public service will be implemented to achieve necessary
  interoperability characteristics.

Whilst Analysis and Design represent distinct use cases, they function
as closely interconnected and often iterative activities within the
architecture development lifecycle. Analysis findings directly inform
design decisions by establishing the requirements that solutions must
satisfy, whilst design activities may reveal gaps or ambiguities in
analysis that necessitate returning to requirements clarification. Both
EIRA and eGovERA support this iterative relationship through their
common vocabulary of Architecture Building Blocks, which provides
continuity between analysis and design phases—an ABB identified as
relevant during analysis becomes a design requirement that must be
satisfied through appropriate SBB selection during design. The
relationship and lifecycle is defined in the Solution Architecture
Framework (SAF).

The role of Architecture Principles
-----------------------------------

Architecture principles play a foundational role in the supported use
cases by the European Interoperability Reference Architecture (EIRA) and
the eGovernment European Reference Architecture (eGovERA) establishing
the fundamental rules and guidelines that govern architectural solution
design decisions. Within EIRA, an Architecture Principle is defined as a
principle that enables general rules and guidelines for the use and
deployment of IT resources and assets across the public organisation.
This definition aligns with established enterprise architecture
frameworks, particularly TOGAF(c) and ArchiMate(c), ensuring consistency
with widely adopted architectural practices whilst addressing the
specific interoperability context of European digital public services.

Architecture principles serve multiple critical functions within the
reference architectures. They provide normative guidance that shapes how
Architecture Building Blocks should be implemented and how Solution
Building Blocks should be selected. They establish constraints that
ensure architectural decisions align with broader policy objectives,
such as data protection, accessibility, or technological neutrality.
They promote consistency across different digital public services by
encouraging common approaches to recurring architectural challenges.

To support public administrations in applying architecture principles
consistently, EIRA and eGovERA leverage the European Library of
Architecture Principles (ELAP). The ELAP is a curated collection of
architecture principles specifically relevant to the design and
implementation of interoperable digital public services across Europe.
Rather than defining principles independently, EIRA and eGovERA
reference and reuse principles catalogued in ELAP, creating a coherent
ecosystem where principles are defined once and applied consistently
across different architectural contexts.

When using EIRA or eGovERA for analysis and design use cases, architects
should systematically consider relevant architecture principles from
ELAP as they make architectural decisions. During analysis, principles
help identify requirements by clarifying what characteristics the
digital public service must exhibit. For instance, the principle of
openness might drive requirements for open data publication or open
standard adoption. During design, principles guide the evaluation and
selection of Solution Building Blocks by providing criteria against
which alternatives can be assessed. For example, the principle of
technological neutrality would favour solutions based on open
specifications over proprietary technologies.

By grounding architectural work in explicit, documented principles
referenced from ELAP, public administrations ensure that their digital
public services embody the values and approaches that enable effective
interoperability across the European public administration landscape.

Diving into core components (ABBs, SBBs, views, and viewpoints). 
-----------------------------------------------------------------

The European Interoperability Reference Architecture and eGovernment
European Reference Architecture are structured around several core
architectural components derived from established architecture
frameworks such TOGAF(c) and ArchiMate(c). Understanding these
fundamental components (Architecture Building Blocks, Solution Building
Blocks, views, and viewpoints) is key for effectively applying the
reference architectures to digital public service analysis and design.

As previously introduced, Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs) and
Solution Building Blocks (SBBs) represent EIRA and eGovERA's adaptation
of TOGAF's building block concept:

- **Architecture Building Blocks** define the required capabilities and
  interoperability characteristics that digital public services must
  possess, expressed as technology-neutral requirements aligned with EIF
  principles.

- **Solution Building Blocks** represent the concrete realisations of
  these requirements through specifications, standards, products, or
  implementations.

This distinction, fundamental to TOGAF's Architecture Development
Method, enables the separation of "what" must be achieved from "how" it
will be achieved, supporting both technology neutrality and practical
implementation guidance. Detailed explanations of ABBs and SBBs,
including their types, relationships, and application, are provided in
subsequent sections of this document.

As already mentioned, the other key aspects and concepts are views and
viewpoints. These concepts are further discussed and described later in
the document. However, find below a high-level overview of both
concepts:

- **Views:** In alignment with both TOGAF and ArchiMate, views provide
  perspectives on the architecture that address aspects of the system.
  EIRA and eGovERA organise their Architecture Building Blocks into four
  primary views corresponding to the interoperability levels defined by
  the European Interoperability Framework: Legal, Organisational,
  Semantic, and Technical (LOST).

- **Viewpoints:** Following ArchiMate and TOGAF conventions, viewpoints
  define the conventions or logics for constructing and using views,
  specifying what elements should be included, how they should be
  represented, and what purposes the view serves. EIRA and eGovERA
  define several viewpoints that enable different analytical and design
  perspectives on digital public services, including the High-Level
  Viewpoint (providing an executive overview of focal ABBs across all
  views), or the Key Interoperability Enablers Viewpoint (highlighting
  critical components for achieving interoperability) amongst others.

The (EIRA) Ontology
-------------------

The EIRA Ontology View provides a meta-level perspective on the European
Interoperability Reference Architecture by formally defining the
conceptual model that underpins the entire architecture. Unlike the LOST
views (Legal, Organisational, Semantic, and Technical) which organise
Architecture Building Blocks according to interoperability dimensions,
the Ontology View articulates the fundamental concepts, relationships,
and structural rules that govern how EIRA itself is constructed and how
its components interrelate.

Purpose and Nature
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The Ontology View serves as the architectural foundation that defines
"the architecture of the architecture." It explicitly models the
meta-concepts that EIRA employs—such as what constitutes an Architecture
Building Block, how ABBs relate to Solution Building Blocks, what
constitutes a view or viewpoint, how interoperability dimensions are
defined, and what types of relationships can exist between different
architectural elements. By formalising these meta-level concepts, the
Ontology View ensures internal consistency within EIRA, provides a
rigorous foundation for extending or adapting the architecture, enables
precise communication about EIRA's structure and components, and
supports tooling development for EIRA validation, analysis, and
application.

This ontological foundation is essential for maintaining EIRA as a
coherent, well-defined architecture rather than an ad hoc collection of
concepts. It establishes the "grammar" and "vocabulary" that govern how
EIRA expresses architectural knowledge, ensuring that new ABBs,
viewpoints, or other architectural elements can be added systematically
whilst preserving the architecture's overall integrity and consistency.

The Ontology view, as mentioned, introduce the most basic and
fundamental concepts and relationships between them. To do so, the view
is organised in two main purposes or aspects: 1) the analysis of a
**European public administration Interoperable Solution**, or; 2) the
design or documentation of a **European public administration
Interoperable Solution**. It important to mention, as the analysis
related content is at higher level, and is focused on explaining and
depicting how ABBs are related to the definition of requirements (ABBs
are requirements), and the definition of these concepts and all related
ones, are key, as they influence and guide the design and documentation
of digital public solutions.

Analysis of an **European public administration Interoperable Solution**
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The **analysis phase** in the EIRA Ontology View defines the conceptual
elements used to analyse a target digital public solution and to
structure the identification of its requirements prior to design. It
captures why a solution is needed, under which constraints, and which
interoperability concerns must be addressed, independently of any
concrete implementation decisions. The analysis phase establishes a
structured problem space that guides and constrains the subsequent
design phase.

More specifically, the analysis phase models how public policy
objectives, constraints, assumptions, and context are translated into
digital solution requirements, including functional, non-functional, and
interoperability requirements. These requirements are derived using EIRA
views, viewpoints, and dimensions, supported by key interoperability
enablers and architecture building blocks. The resulting set of digital
solution requirements provides the basis for architectural decisions
taken during the design phase.

Design of a **European public administration Interoperable Solution** or Documentation of a existing European public administration Interoperable Solution
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The **design and documentation phase** in the EIRA Ontology View defines
the conceptual elements used to specify, structure, and document an
interoperable digital solution based on the outcomes of the analysis
phase. It captures how the identified requirements are realised through
solution building blocks and specifications, while maintaining
traceability to interoperability concerns and policy drivers established
earlier.

In this phase, an interoperable digital solution is modelled as a
composition of solution building blocks, including application
presentation enablers, semantic, organisational, legal, and
infrastructure solutions. These elements are described and constrained
through solution specifications and interoperability specifications,
which may be selected or reused from the EIRA Library of
Interoperability Specifications. The resulting documentation supports
both the design of new digital public services and the documentation of
existing ones in a consistent and reusable manner.

Key Interoperability Enablers (viewpoint)
-----------------------------------------

The Key Interoperability Enablers Viewpoint provides a focused
perspective on the Architecture Building Blocks that are most critical
for achieving interoperability in digital public services. Rather than
presenting the complete architectural landscape as other viewpoints do,
this viewpoint highlights those specific building blocks whose presence
and proper implementation are essential conditions for enabling
effective interoperable operation across organisational and
jurisdictional boundaries.

.. _purpose-and-nature-1:

Purpose and Nature
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The Key Interoperability Enablers Viewpoint addresses a fundamental
challenge that architects and decision-makers face when working with
comprehensive reference architectures: distinguishing between components
that are merely relevant and those that are truly critical for achieving
interoperability. Whilst EIRA encompasses a broad range of Architecture
Building Blocks addressing various aspects of digital public service
design, not all ABBs carry equal weight in determining whether a service
will be interoperable. The Key Interoperability Enablers Viewpoint
identifies and presents those ABBs that function as foundational
prerequisites—the components whose absence or inadequate implementation
would fundamentally compromise interoperability regardless of how well
other architectural aspects are addressed.

This viewpoint organises key interoperability enablers according to the
three interoperability dimensions: Structural, Behavioural, and
Governance. Structural enablers address the compositional aspects of
interoperable solutions, focusing on how components are organised and
shared. Behavioural enablers address the dynamic aspects of
interoperability, focusing on how information and knowledge are
exchanged. Governance enablers address the collaborative and policy
aspects, focusing on the agreements and frameworks that support
peer-to-peer coordination. By organising enablers across these
dimensions, the viewpoint ensures comprehensive coverage of
interoperability concerns whilst maintaining analytical clarity about
the nature of each enabler's contribution.

The RA and related standards and specifications (ArchiMate©, PAAF)
------------------------------------------------------------------

This Reference Architecture developed by the European Commission to
support public administrations on achieving interoperability, and to do
so, the RA is tidily related several standards, specifications, and
frameworks widely adopted for the development of Enterprise
Architectures and Solution Architectures. These are:

- ArchiMate©

- PAAF

ArchiMate© and the RA
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The EIRA© is based on and uses ArchiMate© as the core modelling notation
and language. It is key as ArchiMate© [2]_ is a standardised
architecture modelling notation and language developed and maintained by
The Open Group [3]_.

As an international standard, ArchiMate® ensures wide acceptance and
provides comprehensive coverage of all architecture domains required by
EIRA©, from business and application layers to technology and
infrastructure components.

As an example of the alignment and extension of EIRA© vs ArchiMate©, the
table below shows the mapping between the EIRA© views and ArchiMate©
layers, evidencing the total coverage and alignment:

+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| EIRA© view                    | ArchiMate© alignment                 |
+===============================+======================================+
| Legal view                    | Uses ArchiMate® elements to model    |
|                               | governance, compliance, and legal    |
|                               | constraints                          |
+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| Organisational view           | Maps to ArchiMate® Business Layer    |
|                               | (business capabilities, processes,   |
|                               | actors)                              |
+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| Semantic view                 | Leverages ArchiMate®                 |
|                               | Data/Information concepts to model   |
|                               | data representations, metadata, and  |
|                               | semantic agreements                  |
+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
| Technical Application and     | Maps to ArchiMate® Application and   |
| Infrastructure views          | Technology Layers                    |
+-------------------------------+--------------------------------------+

Furthermore, the machine-readability of ArchiMate® models, which can be
exported in XML format, enables automated processing, validation, and
integration with other systems, supporting EIRA©'s goals of promoting
reusability and interoperability.

Lastly, ArchiMate®'s extensibility allows EIRA© to customise and
specialise building blocks for specific eGovernment contexts while
maintaining compliance with core standards, ensuring that solutions
remain interoperable and reusable across different Member States and
policy domains. The combination of standardisation, completeness,
tooling support, and flexibility makes ArchiMate® a solid foundation for
EIRA©'s mission to enable seamless digital public services across the
European Union.

PAAF and the RA
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The Public Administration Architecture Framework (PAAF), developed by
the Public Governance Institute of KU Leuven [4]_, is a comprehensive
Enterprise Architecture framework designed to model complete public
administrations. Using ArchiMate© as its modelling language, PAAF
enables enterprise architects to represent the entire organisational
landscape—from high-level strategic goals, legal compliance, and policy
objectives down to operational capabilities and service delivery
mechanisms. Critically, PAAF accommodates both digital and non-digital
(manual) processes, making it suitable for capturing the full complexity
of public sector organisations where traditional and modern service
delivery methods coexist.

PAAF and EIRA share a complementary relationship where PAAF operates at
the enterprise architecture level with a broad organisational
perspective, while EIRA© focuses specifically on solution architecture
for interoperable digital public services within the EU context. Both
frameworks use ArchiMate©, enabling natural alignment across eleven
primary architectural elements—including stakeholders, strategic goals,
requirements, principles, capabilities, and digital public
services—though with different levels of granularity. The relationship
can be understood as PAAF providing the "whole organisation" view while
EIRA offers a specialised "zoom-in" on digital public services
interoperability, making EIRA effectively a focused subset within PAAF's
broader organizational scope, with the important distinction that EIRA
exclusively addresses digital capabilities while PAAF encompasses the
entire spectrum of service delivery.

The strategic alignment between PAAF and EIRA bridges the critical gap
between enterprise-level strategic planning and solution-level
implementation of interoperable digital services, delivering value in
both directions. For PAAF users, the alignment provides a clear
methodology to translate organisational strategies and public value
objectives into concrete, interoperable digital service designs using
EIRA's European interoperability framework. For EIRA users, it offers
essential organizational context, ensuring digital solutions support
broader public policies and contribute meaningfully to the
organisation's mission across coordination, regulatory, delivery, and
analytical capacities. This bidirectional alignment enables improved
architectural coherence, enhanced traceability from policy to
implementation, and reduced fragmentation, ultimately empowering public
administrations to pursue digital transformation systematically while
maintaining both organisational strategic alignment and European
interoperability compliance.

References
----------

.. [2] ArchiMate® is a modelling language standardized by The Open Group. More information available at: https://pubs.opengroup.org/architecture/archimate-doc/

.. [3] The Open Group. ArchiMate® Standard and Specifications. https://www.opengroup.org/archimate

.. [4] Public Governance Institute, KU Leuven. Public Administration Architecture Framework (PAAF). https://www.archivesportaleurope.net/
